topic: Mutual Fund and ETF Fees and Expenses
subtopic: Acquired Fund Fees and Funds of Funds
source_evidence: if your fund owns shares of another fund, you are paying the fees and expenses of your fund and indirectly paying the fees and expenses of the underlying fund.
answer: A fund of funds primarily invests in shares of other funds rather than directly in companies’ debt or equity securities. If your fund invests in another fund, you pay your own fund’s fees and indirectly bear the underlying fund’s fees and expenses too. The prospectus fee table lists those underlying costs as Acquired Fund Fees and Expenses when required. Check this item to understand costs associated with the fund’s investments in other funds.
